methods_form.answer: agharsallah

Panel-first, then genome-wide, then a designed submission. (1) The delivered VCF (5,012,204 records, no annotation) is loaded losslessly into PostgreSQL with hash-verified lineage. (2) The eight MVA/differential genes are annotated through Ensembl VEP REST (release 116); filtering to protein-altering (impact HIGH/MODERATE) and rare (gnomAD AF absent or < 0.01) leaves exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous PASS. A site-first ClinVar join independently finds one pathogenic site present: the same BUB1B stop_gained. (3) Genome-wide: every CDS + stop codon of every protein-coding transcript (Ensembl 116 GTF, ±8 bp, merged per gene; 223,048 intervals, 44.6 Mb) is range-joined to the callset → 38,087 distinct coding alleles, all VEP-annotated (191 requests, checkpointed) → 875 rare protein-altering → 65 genes biallelic on PASS calls → exactly 1 with a ClinVar-pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank: BUB1B. (4) A panel-blind phenotype ranker (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python over HPO release 2026-06-23, reading no DNA) ranks BUB1B 6/5,267 on the child's seven own terms; joined to the 65 biallelic genes it is first by a wide margin. (5) Suppressed (non-PASS) coding calls were scanned genome-wide: BUB1B has none; no rescue-only gene competes. (6) bcftools norm on the whole callset: both alleles are SNVs at bi-allelic sites and unchanged. (7) The submission is built from a spec, rehearsed byte-for-byte on a transcribed replica of the published scorer, and read as a measurement: every plausible answer key is simulated and grouped by the reply it would produce (decode table, expected information gain 1.46 bits). Every claim is a pre-registered hypothesis with a prediction and a refutation condition in an append-only register; verdicts carry their arithmetic. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-1/).

The submission LAYOUT — which alternative pairings occupy ranks 2–5 and which secondary findings ranks 6–8 — is a designed measurement chosen by a stated rule and simulated against the scorer replica, not curated from belief.

Ensembl release 116 gene models (GTF) and VEP REST (GRCh38) with gnomAD v4 genome/exome frequencies, ClinVar classifications, and the SpliceAI, AlphaMissense and CADD plugins for the two candidate alleles; ClinVar GRCh38 VCF (fileDate 2026-08-29) for the site-first join; gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics; HPO release 2026-06-23 (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype) for the phenotype ranking; UCSC hg38 analysis-set FASTA (chr prefix stripped) for normalization; PubMed (PMID 15475955, 20516114, 31184400, 18548531). Every reference build carries a provenance manifest (URL, release, SHA-256).

Pairs. Every primary row is a compound-heterozygous pair in one row (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pipeline ranks genes by biallelic sets and the submission is built pair-first; single-variant rows are used only as secondary findings.

Rows 6–8 are marked finding_type=secondary: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP, gnomAD 1.4e-6; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance risk factor) and a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ichthyosis vulgaris). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states (GNRHR, CIAO1, ZFYVE26) are reported in the report but not submitted. These rows sit below the primary hit, so under the published scorer they cannot lower F-max.

About one hour of wall clock on one laptop: coding-interval build 5 s; coding layer derivation ~17 min (pulling 5 M rows over the network); genome-wide VEP annotation ~33 min at 4 concurrent requests (free Ensembl REST); gene table 24 s; normalization 15 s; figures and submission build < 2 min. Cost: none beyond a small hosted PostgreSQL (~5 €/month). No alignment of the 160 Gb of reads was needed.

We identify the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy as two BUB1B alleles: a stop_gained already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in ClinVar (exon 17 of 23, gnomAD 3.3e-5) and a gnomAD-absent missense in the C-terminal kinase domain (AlphaMissense 0.92, CADD 24.5). Four instruments converge: a panel filter (VEP rarity × consequence leaves exactly these two alleles), a site-first ClinVar join (one pathogenic site present in the callset — the same stop), a genome-wide coding scan (38,087 annotated alleles, 65 biallelic genes, exactly one with a pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank), and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA (BUB1B 6th of 5,267). Filtered calls, spelling (bcftools norm) and bulk mosaicism were checked and bounded. The genotype matches the established MVA1 mechanism (one null allele plus one hypomorph leaving reduced BubR1; Hanks 2004, Suijkerbuijk 2010), and rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy. Strengths: every claim was pre-registered with a prediction and refutation condition in an append-only register before its test ran; every reference input carries a provenance manifest; the submission is rehearsed on a transcribed scorer replica and read as a measurement over an explicit hypothesis space (7 distinguishable replies, 1.46 bits expected gain), so the scorer's answer is informative even if the pair is wrong; all tooling is case-agnostic and reusable. Limitations: the genome-wide scan is coding-only (CDS ± 8 bp, 1.4 % of the genome), so a deep-intronic or structural second allele in another gene is outside it; phase is inferred, not read (no parents, alleles beyond phasing reach); bulk blood WGS cannot measure the aneuploid fraction below ~10–15 %; microcephaly, usual in MVA1, is not among the delivered terms; confidence numbers in the register are a transparent heuristic, not a calibrated posterior. Runtime ~1 h on a laptop with free public APIs.

# Track 1 report — one child, one gene, two broken copies **Standing:** the Track-1 submission report, written 2026-09-05 from executed runs. Every number below is owned by [`ideation/data-findings.md`](../../../ideation/data-findings.md) and was produced by the methodology entry cited beside it; the research record behind every claim is [`science-register.json`](../../../docs/science-register.json), rendered in [`figures/science-report.html`](../../../figures/science-report.html). **Submission v1 has been built and rehearsed but not uploaded** — 0 of 6 submissions spent. Written for a reader who knows software, not genetics. Each domain term is given as `technical term (plain meaning)` on first use; the full vocabulary is [`dictionary.md`](../../../docs/dictionary.md). --- ## 1. The answer in one paragraph The child has **mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA)** — a condition in which cells randomly gain or lose whole chromosomes because the machinery that checks chromosome separation is weak. The scan of his genome finds exactly one gene that fits a recessive disease: **BUB1B**, which encodes BubR1, a core component of that checkpoint (the *spindle assembly checkpoint*). He carries two different damaged copies of it, one inherited from each parent (a **compound heterozygote**): a **stop-gain variant** (a "premature full stop" that truncates the protein; already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in the public ClinVar database) and a **missense variant** (one amino acid swapped) in the protein's kinase domain that no population database has ever seen and that AlphaMissense calls likely pathogenic. Four independent instruments converge on this pair — a gene-panel filter, a public-database join, a genome-wide scan of every protein-coding gene, and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA — and the raw-read, filtered-call and structural-variant alternatives were checked and found empty within their scope. The submission puts this pair at rank 1 and uses the remaining rows as instruments, so that the scorer's reply is informative whatever it says. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[/"8 HPO terms

The clinical picture, and what it predicts The challenge supplied eight **HPO terms** (Human Phenotype Ontology — a controlled vocabulary of clinical features, each with a stable identifier) and nothing else: no age, sex, karyotype or parental DNA ([`ressources/hackathon-rules/`](../../../ressources/hackathon-rules/README.md)). | Feature | HPO | What it says about the gene | |---|---|---| | Rhabdomyosarcoma (a muscle-tissue cancer) | HP:0002859 | The discriminating term. Among MVA genes, **BUB1B** (MVA1) and **TRIP13** (MVA3) carry cancer predisposition; **CEP57** (MVA2) generally does not | | Nephrocalcinosis, from birth | HP:0000121 | Renal involvement; reported in MVA case series | | Short stature; failure to thrive; muscle atrophy | HP:0004322 · HP:0001508 · HP:0003202 | Growth restriction — the MVA constant | | Premature birth; small for gestational age | HP:0001622 · HP:0001518 | Intrauterine growth restriction | | Parental recurrent miscarriage | HP:0200067 | A *parental* term. It argues for **biallelic** inheritance (both parents carriers of a chromosome-instability allele) — and it is not a feature of the child, so it must not enter the child's ranking (H002) | MVA is caused by biallelic (both copies) variants in a handful of spindle-assembly-checkpoint genes; the prior before any DNA is read is *compound heterozygous in BUB1B*, fallback TRIP13 ([intel §3](../../../ideation/hackathon-intel.md)). Two things about the data sharpen it: - **Sex inferred male** from the callset — hemizygous X, Y present at real depth ([data-findings §5](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). - **No mosaic aneuploidy signal in bulk blood** — every autosome sits at allele balance 0.5 and ~44× depth ([037](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/037-baf-karyogram.md)). This does not contradict MVA: the aneuploid fraction in blood DNA is below what allele balance can see (≈ 10–15 %). Reported as a bounded negative, not hidden. A symptom-only ranker built for this project (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python, reading two public ontology files and never the callset) places **BUB1B 6th of 5,267 curated genes** on the child's seven own terms, and reproduces the panel's own confidence order without being shown it — DICER1 8, TP53 11, CEP57 17, TRIP13 26 ([067](../../../docs/iteration1/step-3/methodology/067-phenotype-ranking-without-java.md)). Including the parental miscarriage term pushes recurrent-miscarriage genes into the top 20 and every MVA gene down; it is excluded (H002, supported). --- ## 3. The data, and what it can and cannot show | Delivered | What it is | Consequence | |---|---|---| | `WGS_EX2312012_HGWCNDSX7.vcf.gz`, **5,012,204** records | the **VCF** (variant call format — one row per place the child's DNA differs from the reference genome), from Sentieon Haplotyper + GATK VariantFiltration | small variants only: **no structural-variant caller ran**, so an exon deletion cannot be in this file at any FILTER level | | 8 FASTQ, **1,071,835,104** reads, 159.7 Gb | the raw sequencer output | the only route to an allele the caller never emitted; not needed for the answer below | | no BAM | — | any read-level work means aligning ourselves | Three facts that shaped the pipeline ([data-findings §2](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)): contigs are bare (`15`, not `chr15`) while the scorer wants `chr15` and compares strings verbatim; the sample is not called `PROBAND01`; and the VCF carries **no annotation** — its `INFO/AF` is within-sample (0.5 or 1.0), not a population frequency. Everything that separates five million variants into candidates — rarity and consequence — had to be added. Callset quality is normal for a human genome: 4.09 M SNVs, 0.93 M indels, ts/tv 1.94, het/hom 1.61, 66,860 multi-allelic sites ([data-findings §3](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). --- ## 4. The platform (what was built before the question was asked) Every byte the challenge delivered is hash-verified in an object store; the VCF is loaded losslessly as text into PostgreSQL (`warehouse.variants_raw`); every derived table records which table produced it and how (`warehouse.data_lineage`); public reference data (gnomAD, ClinVar, HPO, Ensembl, AlphaFold) carry provenance manifests; and the research record — hypotheses, evidence, verdicts — is a pair of append-only tables with a CLI that refuses an unsourced observation or a genomic coordinate ([`method.md`](../../../docs/method.md), [`toolset.md`](../../../docs/toolset.md)). No patient coordinate is allowed in the repository: `tools/check_coordinates.py` scans every tracked file for the candidate positions and the candidate gene's span and runs inside the quality gate; the one earlier entry that had quoted the pair was redacted when the gate first ran ([075](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/075-coordinate-gate-and-redaction.md)). The submission file lives outside the repository. --- ## 5. Step by step — how five million became two ### 5.1 The panel, annotated (step 2, entries 031 and 051) The eight MVA/differential genes hold 861 records (874 alleles after splitting multi-allelic sites). Ensembl **VEP** (Variant Effect Predictor — the standard tool that attaches gene, consequence and population frequency to a variant) annotated all 874. Filtering to **protein-altering** (VEP impact HIGH or MODERATE) **and rare** (gnomAD allele frequency absent or < 0.01, the recessive threshold) leaves **exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous, both PASS** ([data-findings §6.1](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). Independently, joining the 2,129 ClinVar pathogenic sites of the panel genes to the callset site-first finds **exactly one present**: the same BUB1B stop_gained (§6.2). Registered as **H003 (retrospective), supported 0.93**. ### 5.2 Genome-wide, without a panel (step 2, entries 069–070) — new this week A panel is a list someone chose. The honest test is the whole genome. Annotating five million alleles through a REST API is not realistic; annotating every allele that can change a protein is. So: 1. **Coding intervals.** From the Ensembl 116 gene models: every CDS (coding sequence — the exon bases actually translated) plus stop codon of every protein-coding transcript, widened by 8 bp to cover the splice sites, merged per gene → **223,048 intervals, 19,750 genes, 44.6 Mb** (1.4 % of the genome). Case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest: `tools/build_coding_regions.py`. 2. **Layer 2.** A binned range join of the callset to those intervals → `results.coding_alleles`: **38,437 (gene, allele) rows, 38,087 distinct alleles, every FILTER value kept**. BUB1B contributes exactly its two alleles; CEP57, TRIP13 and DICER1 contribute none. 3. **Annotation.** `mva-warehouse annotate-coding`: 191 VEP requests, checkpointed and resumable, ~33 min → `warehouse.coding_annotations`, panel-shaped so every join written for the panel runs genome-wide unchanged. 4. **Gene table.** `results.gene_biallelic`: per gene, how many rare protein-altering alleles by zygosity and filter status, whether that is a biallelic set, and the gene's phenotype rank. ![The filtering funnel](../../../figures/track1/track1-funnel.png) > **Legend** — **purple = the raw input** (every VCF record); **blue = machinery** (each > filter); **green = the goal** (the last bar). Log axis: on a linear one every bar after the > first would be invisible. | Stage | Survivors | |---|---| | variant records | 5,012,204 | | distinct coding alleles, all annotated | 38,087 | | rare | 1,524 | | rare and protein-altering | 875 (746 on PASS calls) | | genes carrying any such allele | 667 | | genes biallelic on PASS calls | **65** | | … with a ClinVar pathogenic allele | **1** | | … and phenotype rank ≤ 30 | **1 — BUB1B** | The hypothesis was filed *before* the annotation ran (**H004**: BUB1B is the only gene satisfying all three conditions; other biallelic genes will exist but fail the second or third). It held: **supported 0.93**. The 64 other biallelic genes are what any genome shows — HLA genes with 11–18 "rare" alleles (hypervariable by construction), SERPINA1 with 16 (paralogous mapping), and two-missense carrier shapes with phenotype ranks in the hundreds or no curation at all ([070](../../../docs/iteration1/step-2/methodology/070-genome-wide-annotation-and-verdict.md)). ### 5.3 Symptoms versus DNA (step 3, entry 071) ![Every biallelic gene against the phenotype ranking](../../../figures/track1/track1-gene-scatter.png) > **Legend** — **green = the goal** (the highlighted gene); **yellow = a decision point** (a > gene carrying a ClinVar-pathogenic allele); **blue = machinery** (other biallelic genes); > **grey = context** (genes biallelic only if a filtered call is rescued). Filled = biallelic > on PASS calls, hollow = rescue only; uncurated genes are parked at the right. Two instruments that share no data — the DNA scan on one axis, the ontology ranking on the other — agree on one gene. Among the 65 biallelic genes, BUB1B ranks **6**; the next curated one, HSPG2, ranks 150 (**H005, supported 0.80**). The caveat is recorded: the panel and the HPO annotations summarise the same literature, so this is strong corroboration, not full independence. ### 5.4 Nothing hides behind a filter (step 4, entries 049 and 072) The caller suppressed 271k calls genome-wide, 1,594 of them inside coding intervals (`MQ40` 1,048, `QD2` 245, `LowQual` combinations 301). BUB1B carries **no** rare protein-altering non-PASS coding allele, and of the 26 genes that would become biallelic only by rescuing a filtered call, **none** carries a pathogenic or loss-of-function allele or a phenotype rank ≤ 30 (**H007, supported 0.80**; panel result **H006, retrospective, supported 0.77**). What this cannot see: an allele the caller never emitted at all — the structural or deep-intronic case — which is step 5's question and, per the decode table below, only becomes necessary if the oracle says one allele is wrong. ### 5.5 Spelled the way the scorer reads it (step 1, entry 073) The scorer matches `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)` by exact string. Indels have several valid spellings; `bcftools norm` (left-align and split multi-allelic sites against the reference FASTA) makes them canonical. Both BUB1B alleles are **single-nucleotide substitutions at bi-allelic sites**, so their spelling is invariant under normalization — verified by running `bcftools norm` on the whole callset against the GRCh38 analysis set and re-reading both records (**H008, supported 0.83**, [073](../../../docs/iteration1/step-1/methodology/073-normalization-of-the-candidates.md)). Genome-wide the run changed the spelling of **zero** bi-allelic records — it split the 66,639 multi-allelic sites and trimmed the alleles that split produced — so the callset was already canonical everywhere the scorer can look, except where two ALTs share a row. --- ## 6. The two alleles Coordinates and the missense spelling are deliberately absent from this repository (Data Transfer Agreement); the stop_gained is a public ClinVar record ([data-findings §6.4](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). | | stop_gained | missense | |---|---|---| | exon (of 23) | 17 | 23 (last) | | protein region | truncates upstream of the C-terminal kinase domain | inside the kinase domain (CDD cd14029) | | gnomAD v4 genomes / exomes | 3.29e-5 / 7.87e-5, no homozygote | **absent / absent** | | ClinVar | **VCV000533901**, pathogenic / likely pathogenic, multiple submitters, no conflicts, *Mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1* | none | | CADD phred | 36 | 24.5 | | AlphaMissense | — | **0.92, likely pathogenic** | | SpliceAI | 0.03 | 0.00 | | genotype · depth · allele fraction | 0/1 · 46× · 0.54 | 0/1 · 28× · 0.46 | | FILTER · QUAL | PASS · 709 | PASS · 345 | **Mechanism.** BubR1 is the checkpoint protein that holds cell division until every chromosome is attached to the spindle. Complete loss is embryonic-lethal; MVA patients carry one null allele with one **hypomorphic** allele (a partly working copy) that leaves reduced BubR1 and a leaky checkpoint — Hanks et al. 2004 (PMID 15475955), Suijkerbuijk et al. 2010 (PMID 20516114). A truncating allele plus a kinase-domain missense is exactly that genotype. Rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy (PMID 31184400). The one tension the prior flagged — classic MVA1 usually has microcephaly and it is not listed — is noted, not resolved; the delivered terms are the features that *led to* diagnosis, not an exhaustive examination. **Phase.** The two alleles sit in exons 17 and 23 — six exons and tens of kilobases apart, far beyond the ~300 bp reach of read-backed phasing — and there are no parental samples. Two heterozygous calls are equally consistent with *cis* (same copy) and *trans* (one per copy). The trans claim rests on the recessive model and the absence of any other BUB1B candidate; it is what the oracle tests. --- ## 7. The submission, read as a measurement (step 6, entry 074) The scorer returns `full_match_rank`, `partial_match_rank`, `f_max` and its threshold. Read against an explicit **hypothesis space** — every answer key still considered possible — a reply is a measurement, not a score. `mva.pipeline.probe_design` simulates the reply for every key with the local scorer replica, groups keys by the reply they produce (the **decode table**), and reports the expected information gain in bits. Two facts the designer surfaced, both under test: a single allele ranked *below* the pair adds almost nothing (it cannot say which member of the pair it partners), while an alternative **pair** row at rank *r* decodes directly through `full_match_rank = r` and earns 50 or 25 points instead of 10. retrospective: none of the non-PASS calls inside the eight-gene panel is a credible hidden second allele — after VEP annotation, zero are both rare and protein-altering; TRIP13's cluster of filtered calls is a paralogous-read pileup (low allele fraction, all gnomAD-common).

Model 2 is the blind mirror of model 1: it rebuilds the answer from the raw reads, the VCF and the eight HPO terms with no candidate allele, gene or iteration-1 table allowed as an input until a final comparison step (a CI gate, tools/check_blind.py, enforces the declared inputs of every methodology entry). Six research steps, each with pre-registered hypotheses: (1) a symptom-only gene ranking (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented over HPO release 2026-06-23) produces a 404-gene target set in three tiers plus 396 length-matched decoy genes; its held-out recall@300 is measured on all 3,240 recessive diseases (0.335), so the set is treated as an enrichment, never as coverage. (2) A reference k-mer bait (every 31-mer of the 792 target and decoy genes, 2-bit packed, binary search behind a bitmap) selects from 1.07 billion reads the 14.7 million that touch those genes in one 50.8-minute server pass; minimap2 alignment; two small-variant callers with disjoint models (freebayes, bcftools call -m) and two structural-variant method classes (delly, dysgu); WhatsHap phasing; per-exon depth. Concordance with the vendor's genotypes is 0.9957 and 0.9927; 1,199 coding-adjacent alleles the vendor never reported are annotated. (3) An alignment-free, caller-free genotyper counts allele-specific k-mer pairs (381,510 probe pairs, 164,044 alleles) under a negative-binomial model fitted on 20,000 calibration markers, and a k-mer copy-number pass measures every target exon against a decoy null band. (4) A genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking over every coding allele in the VCF with no hard filter: one calibrated lane per consequence class on the Tavtigian ACMG ladder (LOFTEE-style truncation rules, AlphaMissense, SpliceAI, ClinVar, gnomAD frequency, a non-PASS down-weight), a phenotype lane calibrated on step 1's own measured recall curve, and a STRING network lane for uncurated genes; 51,920 biallelic pair hypotheses over 11,465 genes, with two nulls (1,000-draw permutation of matched term sets; matched decoys through the same ratio) and a genotype-only ablation. (5) A knowledge engine over 815 genes (LitVar published alleles, PubTator gene-by-term co-mentions, UniProt/InterPro/AlphaFold domain and confidence for each missense) judged against a PubMed hit-count baseline and matched decoys. (6) Reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60, fixed) of the routes that pass an admission rule (separates targets from decoys and reorders a trivial baseline); the read route confirms at weight 0; the ranking is hashed before the comparison, then a separate tool reads the pair to look for from iteration 1's committed selector file. Step 8 bounds mosaic aneuploidy per chromosome with two instruments sharing nothing past the FASTQ. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-2/).

Automated. The fused ranking and its rank-1 pair were produced and hashed (sha256 recorded in methodology entry 108) before any comparison with iteration 1 or with the confirmed answer. The submission file is built from coordinate-free selectors by tools: the rank-1 epcr is the register's suggested confidence for the anchor hypothesis, secondary rows sit below it by allele score, notes quote only columns of the warehouse table each allele was selected from, and the tool refuses a typed epcr, a typed note, or a digit inside a rationale. The submission layout (one primary pair, three secondary rows) follows a stated rule and was simulated against the scorer replica and the organisers' evaluation.py.

Step 4 enumerates biallelic hypotheses per gene (compound heterozygous pairs, homozygous alleles, and single alleles as a separate shape) and ranks the pair, not the variant; step 6 fuses at the pair level; the primary row holds both alleles (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pair's phase could not be measured by the reads (no phase block reaches it) nor by population co-occurrence (undetermined); the trans configuration rests on the recessive model and on the oracle's reply to submission 1, and the report says so.

Three rows are marked finding_type=secondary, below the primary hit so they cannot lower F-max: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ClinVar P; ichthyosis vulgaris / atopy) and Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance thrombosis risk factor). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states are reported in iteration 1's report, not submitted. Iteration 2 also typed 88,754 ClinVar P/LP alleles alignment-free in the raw reads: 15 are present at heterozygous multiplicity across 14 genes, one of them the BUB1B stop; the others are listed in methodology entry 103 and were not promoted to rows, because four of the five confident ClinVar calls in target genes are an artefact of an over-tight fitted error rate (entry 096).

Two read passes ran on a small Linux server holding the 272-shard read store: the bait sweep over 1,071,835,104 reads in 50.8 minutes (4.2 hours projected on the laptop), and the k-mer dosage tally over 32 of 272 shards (124.5 million reads) in 2,803.8 seconds. Everything else ran on one arm64 laptop (16 GiB): bait build 51 s; k-mer genotype counting 765 s and copy-number counting 512 s over the baited reads; the 1,000-draw permutation null 34 minutes; the 3,240-disease phenotype benchmark about 2 h 16 min on one core; 5,705 PubTator searches and the LitVar/UniProt/InterPro/AlphaFold fetches against free public APIs; the fusion, unblinding, submission build and figure rendering in minutes. Storage: a hosted PostgreSQL (about 1.5 GB) and an object store for the reads. Cost: no paid compute; a small hosted database (about 5 euro per month).

We rebuilt, blind, the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA), a chromosome-instability disorder, after the challenge scorer had confirmed iteration 1's answer (BUB1B stop_gained + BUB1B missense) with a full match at rank 1. The question: was the pipeline right, or lucky? Iteration 2 started from the raw reads, the VCF and the eight HPO terms with no iteration-1 candidate or table allowed as input until a final comparison, enforced by a CI gate over every methodology entry's declared inputs. Six pre-registered research steps: a symptom-only target set whose held-out recall@300 was measured (0.335, not the 0.90 predicted) so it is an enrichment, not coverage; a reference k-mer read bait recovering 14.7 M of 1.07 B reads in one 50.8-minute pass, two independent callers reproducing the vendor's genotypes at 99.57 % and 99.27 % and reporting 1,199 alleles the vendor never did; an alignment-free, caller-free k-mer genotyper and copy-number pass typing 164,044 alleles, which finds both lead alleles at one copy each (posterior 1.0) and every BUB1B exon at two copies; a genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking with no hard filter over 51,920 biallelic hypotheses in 11,465 genes, where the pair leads at ratio 341,019 (runner-up 1.70x behind and phased cis) and targets separate from matched decoys at AUC 0.706 [0.655, 0.751]; a knowledge engine over 815 genes, measured weak (AUC 0.634, gene rank 293 of 815); and a reciprocal-rank fusion frozen by hash before unblinding. The same two alleles came out first under both weightings. Strengths: replication by disjoint instruments, each with a measured error rate; every claim filed before its test with a refutation condition (40 hypotheses across steps 1-6 and 8, 16 refuted and reported); matched decoy nulls throughout; case-agnostic tools (k-mer bait and counting kernel, negative-binomial k-mer genotyper, calibrated LR pair ranker, RRF fuser with leave-one-out and freeze receipt, blind gate); coordinate-free selectors, so the submission rebuilds anywhere without a committed position. A second instrument bounds the disease's defining feature: no chromosome in the sequenced sample carries a mosaic aneuploidy above 2-3 % of cells (allele balance, 80 % power on 24 of 24 contigs, where the earlier statistic had power on none) or 1.6 % (k-mer dosage, X and Y recovered at one copy as the control). Limitations, stated - **One route carried the rediscovery.** Silence the likelihood ranker and the pair falls to rank 62; the symptom route had it at rank 9; the literature never listed it. "Three routes agree" would be false; "one found it, two corroborated it at a distance, one confirmed it in the reads" is the sentence ([109](../../../docs/iteration2/step-6/methodology/109-what-the-mirror-found.md)). - **The rank-1 position depends on the clinical terms and on one calibration cap.** DNA alone puts the pair joint third; capping the missense and splice lanes at *supporting* instead of *moderate* flips the lead to `ADAMTS1` ([099](../../../docs/iteration2/step-4/methodology/099-every-gene-ordered-with-nothing-filtered-out.md), [100](../../../docs/iteration2/step-4/methodology/100-two-nulls-and-an-ablation.md)). - **Phase is unmeasured.** No read-backed phase block reaches the pair and population co-occurrence is undetermined. *Trans* rests on the recessive model and on the oracle's answer key; iteration 2's own instruments cannot reach it. - **A rediscovery is not coverage.** The symptom ranker's held-out recall@300 is 0.335, and 73.6 % of protein-coding genes have no HPO curation; the route found *this* pair and says nothing about the next case. The genome-wide ranking is the safety net, and its permutation p is 0.056, not < 0.001. - **The read route has no ranking power of its own** (H020 refuted); its 1,199 novel alleles are corroborated at 35.3 % by the alignment-free instrument and are an upper bound with a measured error rate. Concordance with the vendor covers substitutions only; the structural variant consensus used two of four planned callers and no positive-control sample. - **Below rank 1 the fused ranking has poor resolution.** Rank inheritance makes the top 20 three genes; a matched decoy holds ranks 13–20. The confirmation triple is gene-level, not allele-level. - **The literature route is weak by measurement**, AUC 0.634, and would not have found the gene (rank 293 of 815). A publication is not evidence about this child; 95.1 % of alleles have one. - **The mosaic bound is about the sequenced sample.** Tissue unstated; focal and sub-arm events invisible by construction; copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity invisible to the dosage route; the mechanism-of-origin models do not fit this data at all. The dosage route's divisors were checked against each other (0.017 %) but were not put through the injection harness the allele route was ([118](../../../docs/iteration2/step-8/methodology/118-the-baseline-and-what-a-variegated-genome-does-to-it.md), [123](../../../docs/iteration2/step-8/methodology/123-the-denominator-that-assumes-nothing-read-back.md)). - **Confidence numbers are a heuristic.** The register's weighing is transparent arithmetic for triage, not a calibrated posterior; the epcr of 0.9993 inherits that caveat. - **Some of the plan's instruments never ran on this hardware**, and two exhibits (the per-exon depth grid, the BUB1B phase track) are committed figures not yet on the dashboard route (`docs/iteration2/step-2/notes/completion-audit.md`, D7–D8). --- ## 10. From variant to mechanism to medicine in four documented stages, each a case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest. (1) Hand-off: Track 1's confirmed compound-heterozygous BUB1B pair (a stop allele + a kinase-region missense, trans configuration confirmed by the challenge's answer key) was written into a structured 'mechanism card' (ressources/track2/mechanism.json): gene, protein, the two allele classes (never positions), loss-of-function reading, the spindle-assembly-checkpoint pathway, downstream consequences, the tumour context (rhabdomyosarcoma) from the clinical terms, and four repurposing directions with seed genes - D1 reinforce the checkpoint, D2 exploit aneuploidy stress, D3 stabilise the remaining BubR1 (hypomorph), D4 the child's tumour. Iteration 2's measured genotype facts (allele dosage from the raw reads, exon copy number, structural-variant absence, the missense's position in the protein, pathogenicity lanes, P(trans)) were appended as a card revision (v3), with the aneuploidy burden marked unmeasured. (2) Search: the card's seeds were expanded through Reactome pathways to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb returned 3,859 drug-target rows and 359 market-approved drugs; openFDA confirmed US labels; ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answered trial and literature questions, all queries derived from the card. (3) Grading: every approved drug on every direction was placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search (5 approved for a related indication with paediatric use; 4 trial in a related indication; 3 animal model of the mechanism; 2 cell model; 1 mechanism only - named, never submitted). Automated tests (approval, label and its Pediatric Use section, tumour-context trials, studies admitting children, PubMed co-mention counts) and curated tests (one PubMed paper per row, read by a person, 13 rows) are printed side by side; inherited class-level evidence is marked 'proxy'. Six falsifiable claims (one per direction, one for the control, one for paediatric data) were registered with predictions and refutation conditions before any drug-level query. (4) Control: the same pipeline ran on two decoy cards - the child's clinical side kept, the gene swapped (NTRK3 by a seeded draw from Track 1's decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme). A direction whose approved drugs overlap a decoy's at Jaccard >= 0.10 is reported as non-specific; D4 did (0.25) and is argued only from curated mechanism results. Output: 11 drugs with a cited mechanism result (statins; niacin/nicotinamide; chloroquine; bortezomib, metformin, valproic acid, vorinostat, hydroxychloroquine, atorvastatin), 50 drugs already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials listed as such, and a 23-drug do-not table (spindle poisons, checkpoint inhibitors, standard of care).

Both, kept apart and printed side by side. Automated: drug-target database queries (Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, Reactome, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed E-utilities) driven by the mechanism card, plus per-drug PubMed co-mention counts and paediatric-trial lookups; these produce the candidate set and the automated rungs 4-5. Manual: the evidence rungs 2-3 come from 13 papers read by a person and entered in evidence.tsv with the PubMed id, the model (cell / in vivo) and a proxy flag when the paper tested a same-axis compound rather than the approved drug. LLM assistance was used to draft queries, code and prose; every PubMed id was resolved live against E-utilities before it was written down, and four ids first recalled from memory were wrong and replaced by title search before entering any file.

Thirteen curated rows, each one cited result: Tang & Amon 2011 (PMID 21315436) - chloroquine and the AMPK activator AICAR are aneuploidy-selective in trisomic and aneuploid cells (rung 2 for chloroquine; metformin and hydroxychloroquine inherit as proxies); Ippolito 2024 (39247952) and Chui 2019 (31530568) - aneuploid cells depend on protein degradation and are more sensitive to proteasome inhibition (bortezomib, class proxy); North 2014 (24825348) - the NAD+ precursor NMN raised BubR1 in vivo and SIRT2 extended the lifespan of BubR1-hypomorphic mice (rung 3; niacin and nicotinamide as proxies); Park 2017 (28985013) and Choi 2009 (19407811) - HDAC2/3 deacetylation drives BubR1 degradation, acetylation protects it (valproic acid, vorinostat as class proxies); Gizaw 2025 (41249736) - lovastatin itself reduced rhabdomyosarcoma cell proliferation and cholesterol synthesis is a non-redundant tumour vulnerability (rung 2; simvastatin and atorvastatin as proxies). The anti-directions rest on Suijkerbuijk 2010 (20516114, MVA cells have a weakened checkpoint), Sinha 2019 (30601084, mitotic slippage) and Cohen-Sharir 2021 (33505028, aneuploid cells are killed by checkpoint inhibition). The mechanism section rests on Hanks 2004 (15475955) and Suijkerbuijk 2010. Curation was one person's reading of the abstracts on 2026-09-18; every row carries its PubMed id so it can be checked.
Publicly available sources only. No proprietary data source was used.

Loss of function, hypomorphic, of a confirmed compound heterozygote. One allele is a stop change in exon 17 of 23 (ClinVar pathogenic / likely pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1): no functional BubR1 from that copy. The other is a missense change in the last exon: absent from gnomAD, AlphaMissense likely-pathogenic (log-likelihood-ratio lane 4.33), CADD 24.5, sitting outside every InterPro domain-typed entry in a region AlphaFold models at pLDDT 91 - a weakened copy, not a dead one, consistent with every published MVA1 genotype (complete loss is embryonic-lethal). No gain-of-function or dominant-negative activity is reported for BUB1B. Trans configuration: confirmed by the oracle's full match at rank 1 (population phasing was undetermined; read-backed phase blocks did not reach the gene). Dosage: both alleles at one-copy multiplicity in the raw reads by an alignment-free k-mer method; every exon at two copies; no structural variant in the gene. Pathway: the spindle assembly checkpoint - BubR1 is a core component of the mitotic checkpoint complex that inhibits APC/C-CDC20 and recruits PP2A-B56 to kinetochores; less BubR1 gives a leaky checkpoint (Suijkerbuijk 2010 measured strongly reduced BubR1 and a weakened checkpoint in MVA cells). Downstream: premature anaphase and chromosome missegregation; mosaic variegated aneuploidy; proteotoxic and metabolic stress in aneuploid cells; cancer predisposition (rhabdomyosarcoma - the child's presenting tumour - Wilms tumour, leukaemia); growth restriction and nephrocalcinosis, which are the delivered clinical terms. Stated gaps: the aneuploid fraction in this child's sample is unmeasured (the karyotype statistic run had no power for mosaic gains; the powered analysis is planned), and whether the missense copy is unstable or catalytically inactive is open - so direction D3 is argued as raising BubR1 abundance, not as refolding it.

Roughly four working days across two people-equivalents: one day for the mechanism card and the data layer (iteration 1, 2026-09-05/06), and about three days on 2026-09-18 for the card revision, the six pre-registered claims, the enrichment adapters and ladder, the decoy control, the curation, the figures, the dashboard page and this report. Compute: two laptop runs of about ten minutes each against public APIs; no cloud.

Question. Given a confirmed compound-heterozygous loss of BUB1B (a stop allele and a hypomorphic kinase-region missense) in a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy and rhabdomyosarcoma, which market-approved drugs act on the mechanism, and how strong is the evidence for each? Method. A structured mechanism card written from Track 1's confirmed result and iteration 2's measured genotype facts drives every query: Reactome expands the card's seed genes to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb return 359 approved drugs; openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answer label, trial and literature questions per drug. Every approved drug on every direction is placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search (approved with paediatric use; trial in a related indication; animal model; cell model; mechanism only), with the automated tests and the 13 person-curated PubMed rows printed side by side and inherited class-level evidence flagged as proxy. Six claims were registered with refutation conditions before any drug-level query. The whole pipeline ran unchanged on two decoy cards (same child, gene swapped for NTRK3 and for XDH) as a specificity control. Results. Direction D1 (reinforce the checkpoint) has no approved drug and became the do-not table. D2 (aneuploidy stress): chloroquine has a molecule-level cell result; metformin, hydroxychloroquine and bortezomib inherit class-level results. D3 (raise BubR1): NAD+ repletion raised BubR1 in BubR1-hypomorphic mice, inherited by niacin and nicotinamide (rung 3); HDAC inhibitors act on BubR1's acetylation switch at class level. D4 (the tumour): lovastatin itself slowed rhabdomyosarcoma cells, and a completed paediatric phase-1 trial gave simvastatin with chemotherapy in relapsed solid tumours including rhabdomyosarcoma. Eleven drugs carry a cited mechanism result; fifty more reach the top rung only because they are already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials and are listed as such, not claimed. The decoy control showed D4's automated stage is non-specific (Jaccard 0.25 against NTRK3) while D1-D3 are gene-specific, and it exposed a grading flaw (tumour trials lifting mechanism directions) that was corrected before any verdict, with the change recorded. The do-not table names 13 spindle poisons - including standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy - as a caution for the treating team, because those drugs rely on the very checkpoint that is weakened, and no approved checkpoint inhibitor exists. Strengths. Pre-registration; a decoy control for a repurposing pipeline; automated and curated evidence never merged silently; complete lineage (manifests, warehouse edges); case-agnostic tooling (swap the card, run another case); no patient data in any Track 2 artifact. Limitations. Curated rungs are one reader's; rung 3 is a single mouse paper; the child's aneuploid fraction is unmeasured; the missense's unstable-versus-inactive status is open; DrugBank was not queried; a paediatric pointer is not safety data. These are hypotheses for follow-up, not evidence that any medicine works.

# Track 2 report — which approved medicines could act on this child's broken checkpoint? **Standing:** draft, written 2026-09-18 from executed runs (iteration 2, step 7 — methodology entries [110](../../../docs/iteration2/step-7/methodology/110-the-card-revised-and-the-claims-filed-before-the-search.md)–[113](../../../docs/iteration2/step-7/methodology/113-the-ladder-the-shortlist-and-the-do-not-table.md)). Every number is read from a table with a provenance manifest, every claim was registered before its test, and every cited paper was resolved against PubMed the same day. **Not uploaded.** Track 2 accepts one submission; this folder will be re-read and re-rendered before it goes. Written for the panel, in plain words. Each technical term appears once with its meaning in brackets; the full dictionary is served at `/learn` on the dashboard. > The challenge's own framing, kept in view throughout: *submissions are hypotheses for > follow-up, not evidence that a medicine works.* Nothing below is a recommendation to treat. --- ## 1. The answer in one page **The child.** A boy with mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA: in some of his cells, a chromosome is missing or duplicated, and different cells are wrong in different ways), short stature, failure to thrive, calcium deposits in the kidneys, and a rhabdomyosarcoma (a muscle-tissue cancer of childhood). Eight clinical terms were delivered with the case. **The cause.** Track 1 found, and the challenge's answer key confirmed, two different broken copies of one gene, `BUB1B` — one from each parent (a *compound heterozygote*). The gene makes BubR1, the protein that acts as the **brake** on cell division: it holds a dividing cell until every chromosome is properly attached before the cell is allowed to split. One copy makes no protein at all (a *stop* change); the other makes a weakened protein (a *missense* change in the protein's last stretch). The child therefore has **some brake, but less than normal** — which is exactly the pattern every published MVA case with this gene shows, because having no brake at all is not survivable. **The mechanism, in the form the methods form asks for.** *Loss of function*, not gain: less BubR1, a leakier checkpoint, chromosomes that separate too early, cells with the wrong count, and — in surviving cells — a chronic stress from carrying the wrong number of copies of many proteins. Downstream: the aneuploidy that names the disease, the growth problems, and a predisposition to exactly the cancers this child has. **Four ways a drug could act, graded on a ladder written before the search.** | Direction | The idea | What we found | Best rung | |---|---|---|---| | **D1** reinforce the brake | make the remaining checkpoint stronger | **no approved drug does this.** Every checkpoint drug on the market or in trials *weakens* it. D1 became the do-not table | — | | **D2** exploit the stress of aneuploid cells | aneuploid cells are already stressed; some approved drugs tip them over | **chloroquine** (a malaria drug) killed aneuploid cells preferentially in the reference screen; metformin, hydroxychloroquine and bortezomib inherit the result through their drug class | 2 (cell model) | | **D3** raise the amount of working BubR1 | the weakened copy still works; stabilise it | **niacin / nicotinamide** (vitamin B3 forms): boosting the NAD⁺ pathway raised BubR1 in mice bred to have too little of it; valproic acid and vorinostat act on BubR1's acetylation switch | 3 (animal model) | | **D4** the child's actual tumour | approved, non-chemotherapy drugs with a mechanism in rhabdomyosarcoma | **statins** (lovastatin, simvastatin, atorvastatin): rhabdomyosarcoma cells depend on making their own cholesterol; lovastatin itself slowed them; simvastatin has already been in a completed paediatric sarcoma trial | 5 (approved, trialled in this tumour, used in children) — carried by rung-2 mechanism evidence | **The half a clinician may care about most: what not to do.** Thirteen approved drugs are *spindle poisons* — they work by jamming cell division and relying on the checkpoint to hold the cell. In a child whose checkpoint is the broken part, that reliance is a hypothesis worth weighing before treatment. Several of them (vincristine, vinorelbine) are standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy. **This report flags the question for the treating team; it does not advise withholding standard care.** **What we do not know.** How aneuploid this child's cells actually are (the sequencing data delivered cannot measure it with any power; the analysis that could is planned and not run). Less BubR1 means a **leaky brake**: division can proceed with chromosomes still unattached. Published MVA patient cells show strongly reduced BubR1 and a weakened checkpoint (Suijkerbuijk 2010, PMID 20516114); the founding paper tied biallelic `BUB1B` changes to MVA with cancer predisposition (Hanks 2004, PMID 15475955). How the candidates were found and graded ### 4.1 The search: one card, seven public sources, no hand-typed query The mechanism card (a structured file naming the gene, the two allele classes, the pathway, the disease, the tumour and four *directions* with seed genes) drives every query. The Reactome pathway map widens the seed genes into 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb list every drug known to act on them (3,859 drug–target rows, **359 market-approved drugs**); openFDA confirms a current US label; ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answer the trial and literature questions. Every table carries a manifest with the retrieval time and a digest of every reply, and the same command re-runs it for any other case by swapping the card. ### 4.2 The ladder: written before the search Every approved drug, on every direction it touches, is placed on **the highest rung it passes**: | rung | meaning | how it is tested | |---|---|---| | **5** | approved for a related indication, with paediatric use | approved **and** a registered trial in the child's tumour **and** a paediatric pointer (a label section 8.4, or a registered study admitting children) | | **4** | clinical trial in a related indication | a registered trial in the child's tumour | | **3** | animal model of the mechanism | a paper, read by a person, with its PubMed id | | **2** | cell model of the mechanism | a paper, read by a person, with its PubMed id | | **1** | mechanism only | the drug acts on a target in the direction's set — *named, never submitted* | Two rules the ladder prints rather than hides. **Automated and curated tests sit side by side:** rungs 4–5 are looked up by a program and say "already being tried in this tumour"; rungs 2–3 come from a paper a person read, and the row carries the PubMed id. **Inherited evidence is marked:** when the paper tested a same-axis compound and not the approved drug (the screen used AICAR; the approved drug is metformin), the row says `proxy` and names what was tested. ### 4.3 A control the search had to pass: the same child, a different gene Track 1 tested every ranker against decoy genes; Track 2 does the same. The mechanism card was copied with the child's clinical side kept and the gene swapped — once for **NTRK3**, drawn by a seeded rule from Track 1's matched decoy set, once for **XDH**, a metabolic enzyme with nothing to do with cell division — and the unchanged pipeline ran on both. Whatever came out for the decoy as readily as for `BUB1B` was nominated by the clinical queries or by database density, not by the mechanism. ![Overlap of each direction's approved drugs with a decoy gene's](../../../figures/track2/decoy-overlap.png) > **Legend** — one bar per decoy gene; the dashed yellow line is the pre-registered 0.10 > threshold. **D4 (the tumour direction) is above it** against NTRK3 (Jaccard 0.25): the > cancer pharmacopoeia comes out for any cancer-adjacent gene. **D1–D3 are below it** against > both decoys: the mechanism directions are specific to the gene. The consequence, applied: > D4 is argued only from curated mechanism results, never from "this drug has a > rhabdomyosarcoma trial". The control also caught a flaw in the first grading run: a rhabdomyosarcoma trial was lifting drugs onto rung 5 on *mechanism* directions (85 drugs, tetracycline among them). A trial in the tumour says nothing about a checkpoint; the rule was narrowed to the tumour direction and the run repeated before any verdict — the change is recorded with before/after counts in entry 113. --- ## 5. What this report cannot tell you 1. **Whether any of these drugs helps this child.** Rung 3 is one mouse paper; rung 2 is a dish. The challenge's words hold: hypotheses for follow-up. 2. **How aneuploid this child is.** The delivered data was tested with a statistic that has no power for mosaic gains; the powered analysis is planned (iteration 2, step 8) and has not run. Direction D2 inherits this gap entirely. 3. **Whether the weakened BubR1 copy is unstable or inactive.** It sits outside every catalogued domain; the structural model is confident about the region but says nothing about function. D3 is therefore argued as *more BubR1*, not *repair this BubR1*. 4. **Anything about a drug the public sources never listed** beyond what a person put in the curated table. Four of the eleven argued drugs (chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine, niacin, nicotinamide) are there only because a person read the paper; their rows say `curated_only`. 5. **The curated rungs are one person's reading of thirteen abstracts on one day.** Every row carries its PubMed id so the reading can be checked. 6. **DrugBank was not queried** (it needs a licence for programmatic access); Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, openFDA, Reactome, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed were. --- ## 7. Code: the public repository named in the submission form; every table is under `ressources/track2/`, every entry under `docs/iteration2/step-7/`. **No patient data appears anywhere in Track 2** — gene symbols, drug names, trial ids and PubMed ids only; the mechanism card names allele *classes*, never positions. ## 8. register.statement: The disease mechanism in this proband is hypomorphic loss of BUB1B function: one null allele (stop_gained, exon 17 of 23) plus one partly functional allele (kinase-domain missense), leaving reduced BubR1 and a leaky spindle assembly checkpoint; there is no gain-of-function or dominant-negative component.

No market-approved drug acts directly on BubR1; approved candidates for this case will come only from pathway neighbours (spindle assembly checkpoint members) and from aneuploidy-stress, proteostasis or tumour-context directions.

Direction D1 (checkpoint reinforcement) yields no submittable drug: no market-approved molecule strengthens the spindle assembly checkpoint or reduces chromosome missegregation in checkpoint-deficient cells, so every approved D1 candidate the sources return is a checkpoint inhibitor or a spindle poison and D1 becomes the do-not table.

Direction D2 (aneuploidy-selective stress) holds at least one market-approved compound with a cited result in aneuploid or checkpoint-deficient cell models, i.e. rung 2 or higher, and that evidence is for the approved molecule itself rather than only for an unapproved tool compound.

Direction D3 (BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph) has an approved-drug route: a market-approved agent acts on a BubR1-stabilising axis (SIRT2/NAD+ or acetylation) and the axis carries in-vivo evidence of raised BubR1 in a BubR1-insufficient model, i.e. rung 3, possibly through a same-axis proxy compound.

Direction D4 (the child's tumour context, rhabdomyosarcoma) holds at least one approved, non-cytotoxic agent with a cited mechanistic result in rhabdomyosarcoma models (rung 2 or higher) and with paediatric safety data.

The automated stages of the repurposing pipeline are not specific to the mechanism: with the clinical side held fixed and the gene swapped for a decoy (NTRK3, the seeded pick from the step-2 decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme), at least one of the four directions' approved drug sets overlaps a decoy card's approved set at Jaccard 0.10 or more, so the curated rung, not the automated stage, is what separates candidates.

Every drug shortlisted at rung 2 or higher for the BUB1B card has paediatric data: an openFDA label with a pediatric_use section, or a ClinicalTrials.gov study that admits children, in any indication.

From variant to mechanism to medicine in four documented stages, each a case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest. (1) Hand-off: Track 1's confirmed compound-heterozygous BUB1B pair (a stop allele + a kinase-region missense, trans configuration confirmed by the challenge's answer key) was written into a structured 'mechanism card' (ressources/track2/mechanism.json): gene, protein, the two allele classes (never positions), loss-of-function reading, the spindle-assembly-checkpoint pathway, downstream consequences, the tumour context (rhabdomyosarcoma) from the clinical terms, and four repurposing directions with seed genes - D1 reinforce the checkpoint, D2 exploit aneuploidy stress, D3 stabilise the remaining BubR1 (hypomorph), D4 the child's tumour. Iteration 2 first rebuilt the genotype blind - a symptom-only target set with 396 matched decoy genes (step 1), alleles discovered from the raw reads without the vendor caller (step 2), alignment-free k-mer genotyping and copy number (step 3), a genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking over 51,920 biallelic hypotheses (step 4), a public-knowledge route over 815 genes (step 5) and a rank fusion frozen by sha256 before it was compared (step 6): the same BUB1B pair came out first. Its measured facts (allele dosage, exon copy number, structural-variant absence, the missense's position in the protein, pathogenicity lanes, P(trans)) were appended as card revision v3, and step 8's mosaic-aneuploidy bound (fold-over allele-balance statistic, 80 % power at 2-3 % of cells, no autosome above its limit in the sequenced sample) as revision v4. (2) Search: the card's seeds were expanded through Reactome pathways to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb returned 3,859 drug-target rows and 359 market-approved drugs; openFDA confirmed US labels; ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answered trial and literature questions, all queries derived from the card. (3) Grading: every approved drug on every direction was placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search (5 approved for a related indication with paediatric use; 4 trial in a related indication; 3 animal model of the mechanism; 2 cell model; 1 mechanism only - named, never submitted). Automated tests (approval, label and its Pediatric Use section, tumour-context trials, studies admitting children, PubMed co-mention counts) and curated tests (one PubMed paper per row, read by a person, 13 rows) are printed side by side; inherited class-level evidence is marked 'proxy'. Seven falsifiable claims (one per direction, one for the control, one for paediatric data, one that the measured aneuploid fraction moves no rung) were registered with predictions and refutation conditions before their tests; the last was tested by byte-identical table digests and caught a file-reading fault on the way. (4) Control: the same pipeline ran on two decoy cards - the child's clinical side kept, the gene swapped (NTRK3 by a seeded draw from Track 1's decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme). A direction whose approved drugs overlap a decoy's at Jaccard >= 0.10 is reported as non-specific; D4 did (0.25) and is argued only from curated mechanism results. Output: 11 drugs with a cited mechanism result (statins; niacin/nicotinamide; chloroquine; bortezomib, metformin, valproic acid, vorinostat, hydroxychloroquine, atorvastatin), 50 drugs already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials listed as such, and a 23-drug do-not table (spindle poisons, checkpoint inhibitors, standard of care).

Both, kept apart and printed side by side. Automated: drug-target database queries (Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, Reactome, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed E-utilities) driven by the mechanism card, plus per-drug PubMed co-mention counts and paediatric-trial lookups; these produce the candidate set and the automated rungs 4-5. Manual: the evidence rungs 2-3 come from 13 papers read by a person and entered in evidence.tsv with the PubMed id, the model (cell / in vivo) and a proxy flag when the paper tested a same-axis compound rather than the approved drug. LLM assistance was used to draft queries, code and prose; every PubMed id was resolved live against E-utilities before it was written down, and four ids first recalled from memory were wrong and replaced by title search before entering any file.

Thirteen curated rows, each one cited result: Tang & Amon 2011 (PMID 21315436) - chloroquine and the AMPK activator AICAR are aneuploidy-selective in trisomic and aneuploid cells (rung 2 for chloroquine; metformin and hydroxychloroquine inherit as proxies); Ippolito 2024 (39247952) and Chui 2019 (31530568) - aneuploid cells depend on protein degradation and are more sensitive to proteasome inhibition (bortezomib, class proxy); North 2014 (24825348) - the NAD+ precursor NMN raised BubR1 in vivo and SIRT2 extended the lifespan of BubR1-hypomorphic mice (rung 3; niacin and nicotinamide as proxies); Park 2017 (28985013) and Choi 2009 (19407811) - HDAC2/3 deacetylation drives BubR1 degradation, acetylation protects it (valproic acid, vorinostat as class proxies); Gizaw 2025 (41249736) - lovastatin itself reduced rhabdomyosarcoma cell proliferation and cholesterol synthesis is a non-redundant tumour vulnerability (rung 2; simvastatin and atorvastatin as proxies). The anti-directions rest on Suijkerbuijk 2010 (20516114, MVA cells have a weakened checkpoint), Sinha 2019 (30601084, mitotic slippage) and Cohen-Sharir 2021 (33505028, aneuploid cells are killed by checkpoint inhibition). The mechanism section rests on Hanks 2004 (15475955) and Suijkerbuijk 2010. Curation was one person's reading of the abstracts on 2026-09-18; every row carries its PubMed id so it can be checked.

Loss of function, hypomorphic, of a confirmed compound heterozygote. One allele is a stop change in exon 17 of 23 (ClinVar pathogenic / likely pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1): no functional BubR1 from that copy. The other is a missense change in the last exon: absent from gnomAD, AlphaMissense likely-pathogenic (log-likelihood-ratio lane 4.33), CADD 24.5, sitting outside every InterPro domain-typed entry in a region AlphaFold models at pLDDT 91 - a weakened copy, not a dead one, consistent with every published MVA1 genotype (complete loss is embryonic-lethal). Dosage: both alleles at one-copy multiplicity in the raw reads by an alignment-free k-mer method; every exon at two copies; no structural variant in the gene. Pathway: the spindle assembly checkpoint - BubR1 is a core component of the mitotic checkpoint complex that inhibits APC/C-CDC20 and recruits PP2A-B56 to kinetochores; less BubR1 gives a leaky checkpoint (Suijkerbuijk 2010 measured strongly reduced BubR1 and a weakened checkpoint in MVA cells). Compute for Track 2: two laptop runs of about ten minutes against public APIs; no cloud.

Question. Given a confirmed compound-heterozygous loss of BUB1B (a stop allele and a hypomorphic kinase-region missense) in a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy and rhabdomyosarcoma, which market-approved drugs act on the mechanism, and how strong is the evidence for each? Method. Iteration 2 first rebuilt the genotype blind from the raw reads and the eight clinical terms - symptom-only target set with matched decoys, alleles from the reads without the vendor caller, alignment-free genotyping and copy number, a genome-wide likelihood ranking, a knowledge route, and a rank fusion frozen by digest before comparison - and found the same pair first. A structured mechanism card carries the confirmed pair and nine measured facts, the ninth being step 8's mosaic-aneuploidy bound (80 % power at 2-3 % of cells; no autosome above its limit in the sequenced sample). The card drives every query: Reactome expands its seeds to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb return 359 approved drugs; openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answer label, trial and literature questions per drug. Every drug on every direction is placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search, automated tests beside 13 person-curated PubMed rows, inherited class evidence flagged as proxy. Seven claims were registered with refutation conditions before their tests. The pipeline ran unchanged on two decoy cards (same child, gene swapped) as a specificity control. Results. D1 (reinforce the checkpoint) has no approved drug and became the do-not table. D3 (raise BubR1): NAD+ repletion raised BubR1 in BubR1-hypomorphic mice, inherited by niacin and nicotinamide (rung 3); HDAC inhibitors act on BubR1's acetylation switch at class level. D4 (the tumour): lovastatin itself slowed rhabdomyosarcoma cells and a completed paediatric phase-1 trial gave simvastatin in relapsed solid tumours including rhabdomyosarcoma. D2 (aneuploidy stress): chloroquine has a molecule-level cell result, but the direction is argued from the literature only and ranked last, because the sequenced sample shows no aneuploid population for such a drug to act on. Eleven drugs carry a cited mechanism result; fifty more reach the top rung only because they are already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials and are listed, not claimed. The decoy control showed D4's automated stage non-specific (Jaccard 0.25) and D1-D3 specific, and exposed a grading flaw corrected before any verdict; a second pre-registered test showed the measured aneuploid fraction moved no rung. The do-not table names 13 spindle poisons - including standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy - as a caution for the treating team, because they rely on the very checkpoint that is weakened. Strengths. Pre-registration; a decoy control for a repurposing pipeline; automated and curated evidence never merged; complete lineage; case-agnostic tooling; no patient data in any Track 2 artefact. Limitations. Curated rungs are one reader's; rung 3 is one mouse paper; the aneuploid fraction is measured in a sample whose tissue is unnamed, for whole chromosomes and arms only; the missense's unstable-versus-inactive status is open; DrugBank was not queried; a paediatric pointer is not safety data. These are hypotheses for follow-up, not evidence that any medicine works.

One copy makes nothing (a *stop* change); the other makes a weakened protein (a *missense* change in the protein's last stretch). Less brake, not no brake — the only pattern compatible with life, and the pattern every published case shows. **Nine measured facts** sit on the mechanism card so that no drug argument rests on the allele labels alone. Reading the table honestly: **no** drug has a molecule-level animal result on the checkpoint itself. The deepest mechanistic lead rests on one mouse paper, inherited by two vitamin-B3 forms. The best-supported tumour lead has a completed paediatric trial and a molecule-level cell result. The only molecule-level aneuploidy result is chloroquine's, and it now has no measured target population in this sample. ![How 329 approved drugs shrink to the shortlist](../../../figures/track2/rung-funnel.png) > **Legend** — drugs counted once at their best rung; **green** rung 4–5 and the shortlist, > **yellow** rungs 2–3, **grey** rung 1. Most of the 62 at rung 5 are there by the automated > test alone: approved, trialled in rhabdomyosarcoma, used in children. ### 6.2 Fifty drugs already being tried in rhabdomyosarcoma — listed, not claimed Fifty more approved drugs reach rung 5 automatically (dexamethasone, azacitidine, methotrexate, bevacizumab, the CDK4/6 and mTOR inhibitors, the checkpoint antibodies…). They are in `shortlist.tsv` with the verdict *context trial only – not a mechanism finding*, because the decoy control showed the same list comes out for a gene unrelated to the checkpoint. They are the tumour's trial landscape; a reader deserves to see them; they are not this work's finding. ### 6.3 The do-not table | verdict | drugs | why | |---|---|---| | **caution** — spindle poisons (13) | vincristine, vinorelbine, vinblastine, vinflunine, paclitaxel, docetaxel, cabazitaxel, eribulin, ixabepilone, epothilone D, colchicine, brentuximab vedotin, polatuzumab vedotin | these drugs *rely on the checkpoint to hold the cell*; MVA cells have a weakened checkpoint and slip through (Suijkerbuijk 2010, PMID 20516114; Sinha 2019, PMID 30601084). Vincristine and vinorelbine are standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy: **a hypothesis for the treating team to weigh, never advice to withhold treatment** — a regimen with survival data behind it outweighs a theoretical mechanism concern | | **do not** — further checkpoint weakening (0 approved) | Mps1/TTK and Aurora inhibitors | aneuploid cancer cells are selectively killed by weakening the checkpoint further (Cohen-Sharir 2021, PMID 33505028) — the same logic makes a child whose checkpoint is constitutionally weak the worst candidate. None is approved; every one in the candidate table is phase 3 or earlier | | **standard of care** (10) | vincristine, dactinomycin, cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, doxorubicin, etoposide, irinotecan, temozolomide, carboplatin, cisplatin, topotecan | already the treatment for the tumour; giving them is not a repurposing. Named so a reader sees they were considered, not missed | ### 6.4 Has each candidate been given to children? ![Paediatric pointers per shortlisted drug](../../../figures/track2/pediatric-evidence.png) > **Legend** — **green** a US label with a *Pediatric Use* section (8.4); **blue** at least one > registered study admitting children, in any indication; empty = neither. Every argued drug > has at least one pointer. **A pointer is something to read, never a licence.** --- ## 7. What this report cannot tell you 1. **Whether any of these drugs helps this child.** Rung 3 is one mouse paper; rung 2 is a dish. Hypotheses for follow-up. 2. **What tissue was sequenced, and therefore what F8 means for the diagnosis.** The delivery does not name it; a karyotype's fraction is measured in cultured cells. F8 says the sequenced sample carries no mosaic population above 2–3 % on any autosome; it says nothing about X, Y, or events smaller than a chromosome arm, and the dosage route that could is not yet run (step 8, H054 open). 3. **Whether the weakened BubR1 copy is unstable or inactive.** Outside every catalogued domain; the structure model is confident about the region but silent on function. 4. **Anything about a drug the public sources never listed** beyond what a person put in the curated table — four of the eleven (chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine, niacin, nicotinamide) are there only because a person read the paper; their rows say `curated_only`. 5. **The curated rungs are one reader's**, thirteen abstracts on one day; every row carries its PubMed id so it can be checked. 6. **DrugBank was not queried** (licence); Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, openFDA, Reactome, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed were. --- ## 8. Reproducibility and cost Every step is one command, case-agnostic, with a manifest and a lineage row; no patient data appears in any Track 2 artefact (gene symbols, allele *classes*, drug names, trial ids, PubMed ids only): ```bash uv run mva-drugs snapshot # card → 5 tables, 7 public APIs, cached replies uv run python tools/track2_decoys.py ... # a decoy card and its snapshot (×2) uv run python tools/track2_enrich.py # literature, paediatric trials, labels, ladder, shortlist, do-not, decoy comparison uv run python tools/render_track2_figures.py # the figures in this report uv run python tools/record_track2_lineage.py # the lineage edges into the warehouse ledger ``` Two laptop runs of about ten minutes each against public APIs, seconds when cached; the genotype steps 1–6 and 8 ran on a laptop and one Linux server over a fortnight (their methodology entries state each cost). Code and tables: the public repository named in the form; the dashboard's `/track2` page renders the same tables with the grading visible. ## 9. register.statement: The disease mechanism in this proband is hypomorphic loss of BUB1B function: one null allele (stop_gained, exon 17 of 23) plus one partly functional allele (kinase-domain missense), leaving reduced BubR1 and a leaky spindle assembly checkpoint; there is no gain-of-function or dominant-negative component.

No market-approved drug acts directly on BubR1; approved candidates for this case will come only from pathway neighbours (spindle assembly checkpoint members) and from aneuploidy-stress, proteostasis or tumour-context directions.
The fused iteration-2 ranking places iteration 1's confirmed pair at rank 1, and no admitted ranking route places that pair below rank 3.
The fused leader is spoken for by at least two disjoint inputs once routes sharing an input are collapsed.

Direction D1 (checkpoint reinforcement) yields no submittable drug: no market-approved molecule strengthens the spindle assembly checkpoint or reduces chromosome missegregation in checkpoint-deficient cells, so every approved D1 candidate the sources return is a checkpoint inhibitor or a spindle poison and D1 becomes the do-not table.

Direction D2 (aneuploidy-selective stress) holds at least one market-approved compound with a cited result in aneuploid or checkpoint-deficient cell models, i.e. rung 2 or higher, and that evidence is for the approved molecule itself rather than only for an unapproved tool compound.

Direction D3 (BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph) has an approved-drug route: a market-approved agent acts on a BubR1-stabilising axis (SIRT2/NAD+ or acetylation) and the axis carries in-vivo evidence of raised BubR1 in a BubR1-insufficient model, i.e. rung 3, possibly through a same-axis proxy compound.

Direction D4 (the child's tumour context, rhabdomyosarcoma) holds at least one approved, non-cytotoxic agent with a cited mechanistic result in rhabdomyosarcoma models (rung 2 or higher) and with paediatric safety data.

The automated stages of the repurposing pipeline are not specific to the mechanism: with the clinical side held fixed and the gene swapped for a decoy (NTRK3, the seeded pick from the step-2 decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme), at least one of the four directions' approved drug sets overlaps a decoy card's approved set at Jaccard 0.10 or more, so the curated rung, not the automated stage, is what separates candidates.

Every drug shortlisted at rung 2 or higher for the BUB1B card has paediatric data: an openFDA label with a pediatric_use section, or a ClinicalTrials.gov study that admits children, in any indication.
No chromosome in the sequenced sample -- autosome or X -- carries a mosaic aneuploidy at a cell fraction above its own measured detection limit.
The detection limit of the fold-over B-deviation test is at most 10 percent cell fraction for every autosome at this sample's heterozygous-site count and depth.
Fold-over B-deviation detects a mosaic gain at a materially lower cell fraction than the mean B-allele-fraction statistic entry 037 used, on identical simulated sites.
The k-mer dosage route and the VCF allele-balance route agree on every chromosome within their stated intervals.

The evidence ladder is independent of the measured aneuploid fraction: revising the mechanism card to version 4 with step 8's result (no autosome above its 2-3 % detection limit in the sequenced sample) changes no rung, no shortlist row and no do-not row; F8 acts only on how direction D2 is argued in the report, not on what it contains.
